description: The Fuling landslide research team publishes an inventory of landslides triggered by heavy rain in Chongqing, China, during 19–25 June 2019. The article reports 791 mapped landslides across Fuling District, with locations, sizes and mapped distribution, covering a combined 818,418 square metres. Researchers interpreted before-and-after remote-sensing images and compiled graphic and attribute databases. The Mendeley Data DOI registry identifies version one and states CC BY 4.0, with free public access; exact file formats should be checked in the repository before importing. Road, power-line and hillside-settlement models can use these event locations to test rainfall-triggered slope exposure or calibrate susceptibility maps. The inventory records one storm and is not a complete long-term frequency record. Small failures or vegetated scars may have been missed by imagery interpretation, and the paper's regional associations should not be treated as causal forecasts. It complements data-ahn-netherlands-elevation-model only as a terrain-related comparison from another country; local Fuling elevation and rainfall data would be needed for a numerical run. No dataset file was downloaded.
